corrections.reason: The independent frozen-label audit confirms that the inherited source and both objects implement a remote service-inventory chain; versions 1 and 2 remain unchanged.

basis: upstream source at each frozen commit
the unchanged version 1 and version 2 review boundaries
digest-bound independent audits for every inherited-label correction
review_policy.comparison: exact label sets after applying only declared audit-bound corrections and combining all three immutable source layers

limitations: Labels describe static capability evidence and loader support, not successful runtime behavior.
Version 3 spans three upstream repositories at exact revisions, so broader ecosystem generalization remains descriptive.
The second blocked family is represented by both upstream-published x64 and x86 objects.
The second positive interprocedural family is x64-only because the pinned upstream Makefile intentionally does not publish its x86 PoolParty build.
PoolParty contains eight selectable injection paths in one object; labels describe object-level static evidence, not execution of every path.

cases.review_notes: The source creates a logon token, inspects its elevation, and passes it to BeaconUseToken. Both published architectures import that unsupported Beacon API and retain the token-context primitives.

The dispatcher selects Inject1 through Inject8. Inject2 opens the target process and calls RemoteTpWorkInsertion, which reads the remote worker-factory pool with ReadProcessMemory. The object also contains dynamic resolution, handle discovery, remote-memory operations, and temporary-file I/O; the latter does not resolve or write a Startup-folder path.
